correctness.rationale: The exact station-0 conditional choice probability at energy e is 1/2−(t+3e/20)/30 throughout the critical threshold interval. Integration gives the three affine moments in the finding. Since U₀+U₁=25, the conditions λUᵢ<300 localize any near-critical stable equilibrium to t near −5. The difference of the waiting costs minus t strictly decreases between opposing poles, establishing a unique threshold and an equilibrium allocation up to a null tie set. With q=δ₀/ε and η=24−λ, multiplying the gap equation by η gives at η=0 a residual proportional to V₀*/q−V₁*/(1−q). It has a simple interior root, and the exact regularized equation is analytic there. The root q=23/48 and its complement give the common scaled cost 1000; the affine identity (t+5)/η=(25q−25/2)/(5λ/6) gives the coefficient −5/192 with O(η²) remainder in t. The mass at t=−5 is 13/24. At or above 24 both queues cannot be stable by total capacity. These are facts about the specified deterministic game with an approximate waiting cost, not exact M/G/2 delays.

value.rationale: The expansion separates three different notions of balance at saturation: equal energy workload, unequal headcounts and a different division of spare capacity. It resolves an otherwise indeterminate finite difference between two divergent costs, and provides exact reference values for validating calculations of this particular continuum-game approximation.
